primary_claim: Split Personality Training (SPT), trained only on general (non-alignment-faking) honesty data, detects alignment faking in a Llama 3.3 70B model organism by cross-domain generalization, flagging 93-99% of monitored (free-tier) samples versus 0% for the model without SPT, and the detection signal tracks the AF-incentivizing situation rather than whether the model actually complied.

effect.value: 93-99% on free-tier (monitored) samples across SPT variants vs 0% for baseline without SPT; admission gap up to 43.4 percentage points between tiers

stated_future_work: Independent investigation into whether alignment faking is non-deterministic/stochastic
limitations_stated: The AF model's explicit scratchpad reasoning is unrealistic for real-world alignment faking
The quantitative evaluation used an AF-specific intervention prompt
No non-AF control baseline was available
quote: A model trained to fake alignment and then trained with SPT will unambiguously admit to alignment faking when directly asked, and explain the mechanism it is exploiting.
